questions.q: Which OWD setting lets any user who can see a Lead or Case also reassign its ownership, not just view or edit it?
options: Public Read Only
Controlled by Parent
Private
Public Read/Write/Transfer
questions.explain: Public Read/Write/Transfer is a special option available on Leads and Cases that adds the ability to change record ownership on top of read/write access — useful for high-throughput, queue-style objects.

questions.q: A detail object in a master-detail relationship has its OWD set to Controlled by Parent. What determines its visibility?
options: Its own independent OWD setting, unrelated to the parent
The visibility of its master-detail parent record
Whichever profile the detail record's owner holds
The role hierarchy position of the detail record's owner only
questions.explain: Controlled by Parent means the detail record's visibility exactly mirrors whatever visibility rules apply to its master-detail parent — it has no independent record-level security of its own.

questions.q: For a standard object like Account, can an administrator uncheck Grant Access Using Hierarchies?
options: Yes, but only if OWD is already Private
Yes, for any object, standard or custom
No — it's permanently enabled for standard objects and can only be turned off for custom objects
No — Grant Access Using Hierarchies doesn't exist for standard objects at all
questions.explain: Grant Access Using Hierarchies is always on for standard objects, meaning the role hierarchy always grants upward visibility for them. Only custom objects let an admin turn this off, which matters for genuinely confidential custom data.

questions.q: An org's internal OWD for a custom object is Public Read Only. What is true about its external OWD for the same object?
options: External OWD must be at least as restrictive as internal OWD — it can be Private, but never looser than Public Read Only
External OWD is always automatically set to match internal OWD exactly
External OWD can be set to Public Read/Write even though internal OWD is more restrictive
External OWD doesn't apply unless the object is also master-detail
questions.explain: Salesforce never allows external (portal/community/partner) access to be looser than internal access for the same object — external users are outside the trust boundary that justifies the internal default, so external OWD can only be equal to or more restrictive than internal OWD.

questions.q: This lesson describes reading the OWD grid as a 'risk register.' What does that mean in practice?
options: Deleting any object whose OWD setting looks unusual
Assuming every OWD setting is correct because Salesforce sets secure defaults automatically
Treating every object set to Public Read/Write as a flag worth questioning — was that choice deliberate, or just an unexamined default?
Only reviewing OWD once per year during a compliance audit
questions.explain: Reading the grid as a risk register means treating permissive settings like Public Read/Write as questions to investigate rather than facts to accept — because every object set that way is trusting all users equally with no per-record distinction, which is worth confirming was an intentional design choice.
